name: STM32WB15CCU6
title: STM32WB15CC: Arm Cortex-M4 MCU with FPU at 64 MHz and a Bluetooth Low Energy 5.3 radio, 320 KB flash, 48 KB SRAM
summary: A two-core wireless microcontroller: the application runs on a Cortex-M4 with FPU at up to 64 MHz (CPU1), while a separate Cortex-M0+ (CPU2) runs the Bluetooth Low Energy 5.3 stack and the radio's low layers. The 2.4 GHz transceiver has an on-chip balun, 1 Mbps and 2 Mbps modes, -95.5 dBm sensitivity at 1 Mbps and up to +5.5 dBm output. It holds 320 KB of flash, 48 KB of SRAM, a 12-bit 2.5 Msps ADC, one comparator, AES, PKA, RNG, one USART, one LPUART, one SPI, one I2C and a touch-sensing controller. It runs from 1.71 V to 3.6 V, with a step-down SMPS on the UFQFPN48 and WLCSP49 parts and none on the UFQFPN48E (extended I/O) part.

Order code fields (STM32 WB 15 C C U 6 E TR): WB = wireless Bluetooth; 15 = die 1, full feature set; first C = 48 pins or 49 balls; second C = 320 Kbytes flash; U = UFQFPN48 7 x 7 mm, Y = WLCSP49 0.4 mm pitch; 6 = -40 to 85 °C ambient (105 °C junction), 7 = -40 to 105 °C ambient (125 °C junction); E = extended I/O option, UFQFPN48 only; TR = tape and reel, xxx = programmed parts. notes: (1) Y = enabled; O = optional (off by default, software can turn it on); R = data retained; - = not available. Wake-up capability: whether the function can wake the device from that mode.

(8) In Shutdown, each I/O can be set to pull-up, pull-down or floating; that setting does not survive the exit from Shutdown.

operation.text: Two cores share the chip. CPU1, a Cortex-M4 with FPU, MPU and DSP instructions at up to 64 MHz, runs the application. CPU2, a Cortex-M0+, runs the whole Bluetooth Low Energy stack with the RF front end and dedicated peripherals. They share the flash, the three SRAMs, RNG, PKA, the clock controller and power control, and talk through the IPCC (six bidirectional channels) and the HSEM hardware semaphores. The device always boots on CPU1.

320 KB of flash with ECC (single-error correction, double-error detection) is shared by time between the two CPUs; part of it is reserved for CPU2 and cannot be reached by CPU1. The ART accelerator (prefetch queue and branch cache on the 64-bit flash) gives the equivalent of zero-wait-state execution up to 64 MHz. SRAM is 48 KB: SRAM1 12 KB at 0x2000 0000; SRAM2a 32 KB at 0x2003 0000, mirrored at 0x1000 0000; SRAM2b 4 KB at 0x2003 8000, mirrored at 0x1000 8000. SRAM2a/2b have parity, can be write-protected in 1 KB steps and partly belong to CPU2. All SRAM runs at zero wait states at any clock. A 1 KB OTP area and 20 backup registers (80 bytes) are also present.

Readout protection RDP has three levels: 0 none; 1 blocks flash access while debug, SRAM boot or the bootloader is used; 2 permanently disables debug, SRAM boot and bootloader. Write protection covers two areas in 4 KB steps. PCROP makes two areas execute-only in 2 KB steps, with an option bit choosing whether they are erased on an RDP 1 to 0 change. The MPU offers eight regions of eight subregions, 32 bytes to 4 GB.

Blocks: secure flash and SRAM partitions for the RF subsystem only; true RNG giving 32-bit numbers; AES-256 accelerator with ECB, CBC, CTR, GCM, GMAC and CCM; PKA for modular exponentiation up to 3136-bit modulus and ECC scalar multiplication, ECDSA sign and verify up to 521 bits; CRC unit; 96-bit unique ID and IEEE 64-bit unique ID from which a 48-bit Bluetooth EUI can be derived. Secure firmware installation covers the radio stack.

The BOOT0 pin (PH3) and the BOOT1 option bit select user flash, system memory or embedded SRAM at start-up. The bootloader in system memory accepts USART (PA9/PA10), SPI (PA4 to PA7) and I2C (PB6/PB7), and supports secure firmware update.

A 2.4 GHz Bluetooth Low Energy 5.3 transceiver at 1 or 2 Mbps. Transmission modulates the carrier directly; reception uses a low-IF chain with AGC at RF and IF. An internal transformer and balun let RF1 drive a single-ended antenna of about 50 Ω, and its band-pass shape eases harmonic and blocker filtering. Output power is set through the PA's LDO, from -20 dBm to +5.5 dBm in 1 dB steps, with smooth ramping. The 32 MHz crystal needs no external capacitors: two programmable internal banks (XOTUNE, 6 bits) trim it. RF_TX_MOD_EXT_PA (PB0) can key an external PA. With the SMPS, the peak radio current at +5.5 dBm is 7.4 mA, within coin-cell limits. Integrated passive companion chips (MLPF-WB-01E3, MLPF-WB55-02E3, MLPF-WB-02D3) are offered for the matching.

The stack on CPU2 supports GAP central, peripheral, observer and broadcaster; ATT/GATT client and server; SM; L2CAP; link-layer AES-128; several simultaneous roles; LE data packet length extension (application throughput up to about 800 kbps); privacy 1.2; secure connections with ECDH; 2 Mbps PHY. Topologies: piconet master with up to eight slaves; scatternet master with up to six slaves while slave to two masters, or four slaves while slave to four masters; slave to up to eight masters. The stack can be updated in the field.

VDD (1.71 V to 3.6 V) powers the I/Os, regulators, RF, SMPS, reset, power management and clocks; VDDRF and VDDSMPS must always be wired to VDD. VDDA (1.62 V to 3.6 V with ADC or comparator in use) feeds the ADC and comparator, may differ from VDD and is tied to VDD when unused. VBAT (1.55 V to 3.6 V) keeps the RTC, LSE, backup registers and one tamper pin alive when VDD is gone; switching to VBAT is automatic. On packages without a VBAT pin the backup domain runs from VDD. An internal VBAT charger (5 kΩ or 1.5 kΩ) can be enabled while VDD is present.

While VDD is under 1 V, VDDA must stay below VDD + 300 mV; above 1 V the supplies are independent. During power-down VDD may fall below the other supplies only if the energy delivered to the chip stays under 1 mJ. VDD, VDDRF and VDDSMPS are wired together so they follow the same sequence.

The UFQFPN48 (STM32WB15CCU) and WLCSP49 have a step-down SMPS; the UFQFPN48E has none. Out of reset it is in bypass. It can be turned on or bypassed by software at any time (for accurate ADC readings, for example), and can drop into bypass automatically when VDD falls below a chosen BOR level (BOR1 to BOR4; default 2.0 V). With VDD below 1.95 V it is left off or forced to bypass. Without the SMPS, VDDSMPS, VLXSMPS and VFBSMPS all go to VDD. Its characteristics are given at a 4 MHz clock with 10 µH and 4.7 µF. VFBSMPS may range from 1.4 V to 3.6 V; TX power figures use 1.7 V (maximum power) or 1.4 V (0 dBm).

Three linear regulators: the main regulator (Run, Sleep, Stop 0), the low-power regulator (Low-power run, Low-power sleep, Stop 1, and SRAM retention in Standby) and the RF regulator, run by the RF subsystem. All are off in Standby and Shutdown. Dynamic voltage scaling sets VCORE to the frequency in use. In Low-power run the CPU is limited to 2 MHz and the RF subsystem is unavailable.

The brown-out reset is on in every mode except Shutdown; the lowest level, BOR0, is about 1.66 V rising, 1.64 V falling, and higher levels BOR1 to BOR4 (2.0 V to 2.9 V) are chosen by option byte, so no external reset circuit is needed. The PVD compares VDD with one of seven thresholds (2.05 V to 2.98 V) or the PVD_IN pin and can interrupt on either crossing. PVM3 watches VDDA against about 1.65 V.

Sleep stops only CPU1. Low-power run and Low-power sleep use the low-power regulator, limit CPU1 to 2 MHz and need the RF subsystem off. Stop 0 (main regulator on, 1.7 µs wake-up) and Stop 1 (3.05 µA, 4.7 µs) keep all SRAM and registers; the radio can wait for events in either, and the wake-up clock must be HSI16 when the RF subsystem is in use. Standby keeps BOR, optionally the RTC and, through the low-power regulator, all 48 KB of SRAM; it wakes on NRST, IWDG, WKUP pins PA0/PA2, RTC events or LSE CSS, restarting on HSI16. Shutdown (12 nA) keeps only the backup domain, has no BOR, wakes on NRST, WKUP pins or RTC, and restarts on the 4 MHz MSI. Standby and Shutdown cannot be used during radio activity. The chip's actual power state is the higher of what CPU1 and the RF subsystem each ask for.

During and after reset the I/Os sit in analog state with Schmitt triggers off, to save current; the internal reset pull-up is turned off when the reset comes from inside. NRST has a permanent pull-up of about 40 kΩ and a filter that ignores pulses under 70 ns and passes those over 350 ns. NRST can be configured as GPIO PB11.

Sources: HSE 32 MHz crystal with trimming (needed by the radio); HSI16 16 MHz RC (±1 % over 0 °C to 85 °C); MSI 100 kHz to 48 MHz in 12 ranges, trimmed by the LSE to better than ±0.25 %; LSE 32.768 kHz crystal with four drive levels or bypass; LSI1 32 kHz (±5 %), which also clocks the IWDG; LSI2 32 kHz, untrimmable but stable to ±200 ppm/°C, usable by the radio instead of the LSE. One PLL fed by HSE, HSI16 or MSI gives up to 64 MHz with separate P, Q and R outputs (ADC, RNG). SYSCLK can be HSI16, MSI, HSE or PLL. After reset the chip runs on the 4 MHz MSI. AHB and APB run up to 64 MHz. The clock security system moves to HSI16 if the HSE fails and can also flag an LSE failure. MCO outputs an internal clock; LSCO outputs LSI or LSE in every low-power mode down to Standby.

Up to 37 I/Os (35 of them 5 V tolerant), each configurable as push-pull or open-drain output, input with or without pull-up/pull-down, alternate function or analog; the configuration can be locked. They sit on AHB2 for fast toggling. Each sinks or sources up to ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed levels. PC14 and PC15 run through the backup switch: 2 MHz, 30 pF and no current sourcing. PB0 and PB1 are 3.6 V tolerant (TT) and should run at the lowest speed setting during RF operation. AT0 and AT1 are left unconnected.

An input held at an intermediate level draws current through its Schmitt trigger; an input left floating can drift there or toggle from noise. Unused pins are set to analog mode, or given a defined level by a pull resistor or by making them outputs. ADC input pins are configured as analog.

One DMA with seven channels; the DMAMUX routes any peripheral request to any channel. Four software priority levels, byte/half-word/word transfers, circular buffers, up to 65536 items, memory-memory, memory-peripheral and peripheral-peripheral. The NVIC handles up to 63 maskable interrupts with 16 priority levels; the EXTI handles wake-up events and interrupts to both CPUs.

12-bit SAR ADC, up to 2.5 Msps at 12 bits (4.38 Msps at 6 bits), with up to ten external channels and three internal ones: temperature sensor (ADC1_IN12), VREFINT (ADC1_IN13) and VBAT through a divide-by-3 bridge. Single and scan modes, analog watchdog. VREF+ is VDDA inside. Below VDDA = 2.4 V the I/O analog switch booster must be enabled. A calibration after each power-up is recommended. Negative current injected into an analog pin degrades conversions on the others; a Schottky diode from pin to ground protects pins that may see it.

The temperature sensor output is linear with temperature, about 2.5 mV/°C and 0.76 V at 30 °C; each part is calibrated at 30 °C and 130 °C with VDDA = 3.0 V (TS_CAL1, TS_CAL2). VREFINT, about 1.212 V, is measured per part at 30 °C and VDDA = 3.6 V (VREFINT_CAL) and serves the ADC and comparator.

One ultra-low-power comparator with selectable speed/power, hysteresis and output polarity. The reference is an I/O, VREFINT, or 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 of VREFINT. It can wake the chip from Stop, interrupt, and break or trigger the timers.

The touch controller measures capacitance by surface charge transfer, with one sampling capacitor serving a group of channels. Channels: 8 on the UFQFPN48E, 3 on the UFQFPN48, 2 on the WLCSP49. Spread spectrum, programmable charge-transfer frequency and a maximum-count limit are provided; the STMTouch library drives it.

TIM1: 16-bit advanced timer, four channels, three complementary outputs with dead time, break inputs. TIM2: 32-bit, four channels, encoder support. LPTIM1 and LPTIM2: 16-bit, run in Stop 0 and Stop 1 from LSE, LSI, HSI16, APB or an external clock and can wake the chip; LPTIM1 has encoder mode. IWDG: 12-bit down-counter with 8-bit prescaler on LSI, works in Stop and Standby. WWDG: 7-bit, early-warning interrupt. SysTick: 24-bit.

BCD calendar with sub-seconds, two alarms, 17-bit wake-up timer, digital calibration to 0.95 ppm, smooth correction, reference clock (50/60 Hz) input, timestamp and one tamper pin. Clock: LSE, LSI1, LSI2 or HSE/32. With the LSE it runs in every mode including VBAT; with an LSI it stops in Shutdown and VBAT. The 20 backup registers survive system reset and Standby/Shutdown wake-up.

I2C1: Standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus (20 mA drive pins), SMBus/PMBus, independent clock, wake-up from Stop on address match; its pins are not true open-drain (the PMOS is disabled but present). USART1: up to 4 Mbit/s, IrDA, smartcard (ISO 7816), LIN, RS485 DE, SPI master mode, wake-up from Stop at up to 200 kbaud. LPUART1: up to 9600 baud from the LSE alone, wake-up from Stop at up to 220 kbaud. SPI1: 32 Mbit/s master, 24 Mbit/s slave, 4- to 16-bit frames, NSS pulse, TI mode, CRC. All can use DMA.

The SWJ-DP offers JTAG or two-wire SWD; SWDIO and SWCLK share PA13 and PA14 with JTMS and JTCK, freeing the other JTAG pins for other uses. Out of reset PA13, PA14, PA15, PB3 and PB4 are debug pins with pull-ups (pull-down on PA14). The WLCSP49 offers SWD only.

Every supply pair (VDD/VSS, VDDRF/VSSRF and the rest) is decoupled with ceramics placed as close as possible to the pins or directly beneath them on the far side. The 10 nF on VDDA is a good-quality ceramic next to the chip. The exposed pad of the UFQFPN48 and the VSSRF pins go to the ground plane; this is needed for correct RF operation. RF1 and the 32 MHz oscillator pins follow the nominal reference layout (AN5165). The 32.768 kHz crystal and its capacitors sit as close to the pins as possible.

The chip reaches class 3B for ESD on I/Os and 5A for fast transient bursts on the supplies at 64 MHz. Holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for one second reproduces the usual failures (unexpected reset, program counter corruption) for software hardening trials.

At TA = 82 °C, IDD = 50 mA at 3.5 V, 20 outputs sinking 8 mA at 0.4 V and 8 sinking 20 mA at 1.3 V: PINT = 175 mW, PI/O = 272 mW, PD = 447 mW, so on the UFQFPN48 (27.7 °C/W) TJ = 94 °C, which suits suffix 6. At TA = 102 °C with IDD = 20 mA and 20 outputs at 8 mA: PD = 134 mW, TJ = 106 °C, which needs suffix 7.
